# Civgraph

> Civgraph (https://civgraph.net) is an interactive atlas of the geography, administrative history, and statistics of Ireland and Northern Ireland — 1,000+ map layers (boundaries, electoral areas, townlands, physical features, thematic data) plus a large catalogue of statistical sources and a semantic knowledge graph.

The website is a MapLibre GL (WebGL) single-page app: map features are rendered on the GPU, **not** in the DOM. Do not try to read features by scraping the page or driving the UI — you will get stuck at an empty app shell. Instead, use the public, machine-readable data described below. All of it is static and fetchable over HTTPS with no authentication.

## For AI agents: start here

- [Agent guide](https://civgraph.net/agent/guide.md): how to find maps, fetch geometry, and — the common task — determine which features on one map correspond to features on another (spatial join). Includes a copy-paste Python recipe.
- [Map catalogue (slim, for agents)](https://civgraph.net/agent/maps-index.json): every map layer with its `id`, `name`, `category`, `provider`, `bounds`, `labelProperty`, and a direct link to its geometry file. Prefer this over the full catalogue.

## Data

- Geometries are **FlatGeobuf** (`.fgb`, CRS **EPSG:4326**) served from `https://data.civgraph.net/data/maps/…`. FlatGeobuf is readable by GDAL/OGR, GeoPandas/pyogrio, and the flatgeobuf JS/Python libraries, and supports HTTP range requests (bbox-filtered reads) for large layers.
- [Full map catalogue](https://civgraph.net/data/database/maps.json): the complete `maps.json` (larger; the slim index above is preferred for agents).
- **Statistical overlays** (census, NIMDM deprivation): the `dataOverlays` array in [`agent/maps-index.json`](https://civgraph.net/agent/maps-index.json) lists value tables — each a CSV (e.g. `data/census/derived/…`) joined to a map layer by a key column. Fetch the CSV directly for the numbers (population, age, religion, NS-SeC social grade, deprivation rank, …), or join it to the layer geometry. Covers 2021 Census (LGD/Ward/Settlement/Data Zone), 2011 Census (Small Area), and NIMDM 2017 deprivation (Small Area).
- **2021 Census tables (NISRA flexible table builder):** a mirror of 147,492 tables (datasets `PEOPLE` and `HOUSEHOLD`) at NI geographies LGD/DEA/Super-Data-Zone/Data-Zone — the complete set of crosstabs NISRA disclosure control will release, harvested exhaustively up to 5-way (every univariate, 2-, 3-, 4- and 5-way combination that passes, plus the ready-made tables), as gzipped CSVs. Index: [`data/census/nisra-ftb/manifest.json`](https://data.civgraph.net/data/census/nisra-ftb/manifest.json); guide: [`agent/nisra-ftb-README.md`](https://civgraph.net/agent/nisra-ftb-README.md). Read counts directly instead of driving the Cantabular UI.
- **2001 Census (NISRA bulk download):** the full 2001 bulk tables in two layers — pristine originals (10 ZIPs at `data/census/2001-bulk/originals/`) and **2,606 cleaned tables** in the same tidy schema as the 2021/2011 corpora (`Geography Code, Geography Label, Category 1…k, Count`), indexed by [`data/census/2001-cleaned/manifest.json`](https://data.civgraph.net/data/census/2001-cleaned/manifest.json). Guide: [`agent/census-2001-README.md`](https://civgraph.net/agent/census-2001-README.md). Key/Univariate/Standard/Census-Area-Statistics/Migration tables at Output Area, Ward, District, NI and admin geographies.
- **2011 Census (NISRA bulk download):** the full 2011 bulk tables in two layers — pristine originals (8 ZIPs at `data/census/2011-bulk/originals/`) and **1,565 cleaned tables** melted into the same tidy schema as the 2021 corpus (`Geography Code, Geography Label, Category 1…k, Count`), one gzipped CSV per table×geography, indexed by [`data/census/2011-cleaned/manifest.json`](https://data.civgraph.net/data/census/2011-cleaned/manifest.json). Guide: [`agent/census-2011-README.md`](https://civgraph.net/agent/census-2011-README.md). Covers Key/Quick Statistics + Detailed/Local Characteristics at Small Area, Super Output Area, Ward, Assembly Area and higher geographies.
- **MRP / small-area estimation:** [`agent/mrp-frame-README.md`](https://civgraph.net/agent/mrp-frame-README.md) documents the 2011 Small-Area poststratification inputs — published joint margins (age×religion, sex×religion) plus the marginals — and how to rake them into a full age×sex×religion×NS-SeC frame. The 2021 3-way joints in the flexible-table-builder mirror above are additional raking margins.
- Some very large layers are served as **chunked** FlatGeobuf rather than a single file; those appear in the catalogue without a single `geometry.url`. Most layers (686 of ~1,014) have a single fetchable `.fgb`.

## Task: feature correspondence between two maps

To answer "which features on map A correspond to features on map B" (e.g. which District Electoral Area each townland falls in, or how 1993 and 2012 boundaries relate):

1. Look up both maps by name/category in `agent/maps-index.json` and read each `geometry.url`.
2. Fetch both `.fgb` files.
3. Run a spatial join with the appropriate predicate — containment for nested administrative hierarchies (townland ⊂ DEA ⊂ county), area-overlap for same-level different-vintage boundaries.

The [agent guide](https://civgraph.net/agent/guide.md) has a working, tested implementation.

## Licence & attribution

Layers carry per-source licences and attribution in the catalogue (`provider`, and `references`/`license` in the full `maps.json`) — commonly OGL v3.0 (NI / OSNI) and CC-BY 4.0 (Tailte Éireann / OSi). Attribute the original providers when reusing data.
